answer: Admission takes one hardware token per identity: a secure element set in a marble block, its secret accreting like a pearl, one hash layer per epoch bound to seed and counter, so the live key never leaves the element and cannot be copied. Enrollment scans the vein pattern, which no second block reproduces; presentation windows drift like a dune, set by epoch seed, moving hourly, so responses cannot be pre-staged. Verifiers check the certificate chain, vein scan, and layer count against epoch age. One token costs 25 dollars once; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 blocks, each presented live every hour.
